title: The Mysterious 'Hum' Heard Around the World May Be Explained
hook: For decades, people worldwide have reported hearing a mysterious low hum with no external source. New research points to an internal explanation: low-frequency tinnitus that only feels external.
key_points: "The Hum" is a mysterious low-frequency sound reported by people worldwide for decades, often with no identifiable external source.
Researchers tested whether people who hear it have exceptional low-frequency hearing, or produce measurable sounds inside their own ears.
Neither explanation fit most participants who reported hearing the Hum.
The strongest remaining explanation is that many cases are a form of low-frequency tinnitus — a sound generated internally that nonetheless feels like it's coming from outside.
content_html: For decades, people around the world have reported a mysterious low hum with no clear source — audible to some, undetectable to everyone around them. It's spawned decades of theories, from secret machinery to seismic activity. A new study takes a more personal angle: maybe the source isn't external at all.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, researchers tested two leading hypotheses about people who hear the Hum: that they have exceptionally sensitive low-frequency hearing, or that their own ears produce measurable sounds (known as otoacoustic emissions). Neither explanation held up for most participants. The strongest remaining possibility is that many cases of the Hum are a form of low-frequency tinnitus — a sound generated internally, within the auditory system itself, that nonetheless feels like it's coming from somewhere outside. It doesn't solve every reported case, but it reframes a decades-old mystery as, plausibly, a hearing-health phenomenon rather than an undiscovered external noise source.

related.title: That Ringing in Your Ears Can Be an Early Warning
related.hook: Hearing loss rarely arrives as silence. It often shows up first as ringing in the ears or a struggle to follow conversation in a noisy room — signs worth heeding early.

related.title: Protecting Your Hearing
related.hook: Noise-induced hearing loss is permanent — once those tiny inner-ear cells die, they don't grow back. The good news: it's almost entirely preventable.
